newsitem.title: TURKEY: IMF to visit Turkey for talks on economic plan.
newsitem.headline: IMF to visit Turkey for talks on economic plan.

text.p: A team from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) will visit Turkey on October 14 to hold talks on Turkey's economic programme, state minister Ufuk Soylemez said on Saturday.

The government would try to secure the IMF's backing for its economic plans, Soylemez told reporters at Istanbul's airport on his return from the United States where he met with officials from the World Bank, IMF and rating agencies.
His remarks were carried by the state-run Anatolian news agency.
Officials say Turkey is seeking to reach an accord with the IMF for a new stand-by arrangement which they believe will increase confidence in the Turkish economy in international financial markets.
Soylemez said Turkey had to lower inflation, realise structural reforms, close budget deficits and provide stability in fiscal policies.

"For this reason, the government should reach an accord on a programme to be implemented and this programme should receive support from international financial institutions," Soylemez was quoted as saying.
